the development, implementation and evaluation of an evidence-based, multi-component, group intervention for the management of anxiety in breast cancer patients.

a multiple‐component group intervention combining support with cognitive and hypnosis components is superior to a single‐component group based on support alone in improving anxiety regulation in breast cancer patients at the beginning of survivorship.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SGI and the MGI had comparable benefits in terms of improvement of anxiety regulation.
we found that the SGI was effective in decreasing anxiety and improving the quality of life of patients with breast cancer during the survivorship period.
the MGI is a better choice for patients with breast cancer who are at the beginning of their survivorship period and who need to learn how to manage their anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MGI was more efficient than the SGI in reducing state and trait anxiety and in promoting anxiety coping strategies, as well as in reducing the use of anxiety‐related drugs, and that the SGI was more efficient in reducing depression, in increasing quality of life, and in improving the perception of the body.
we have shown the benefits of a multiple‐component intervention for anxiety regulation in breast cancer patients at the beginning of their survivorship period.

we need to be careful in how we use the terms “cognitive behavioral therapy” or “cognitive behavioral techniques” in the context of breast cancer, because there are different ways of understanding what these terms mean.
